hint.doors: Open and close each door and check it latches. Look for holes, dents, chipped paint, and loose or broken handles, locks and door stops.
hint.walls: Look for marks, scuffs, holes, hooks and picture nails, cracks, peeling or chipped paint, and any water stains.
hint.ceiling: Look for cracks, stains, sagging, peeling paint, cobwebs and any sign of a leak or mould.
hint.floor: Check carpet for stains, burns, worn patches and loose edges. Check hard floors for scratches, chips, lifting boards and cracked tiles.
hint.windows: Check each window opens, closes and locks. Look for cracked glass, broken latches, torn or missing flyscreens and damaged sills.
hint.window_coverings: Open and close them. Look for broken slats, missing cords or wands, stains, fading, and damaged tracks or rods.
hint.lights: Turn every light on and off. Note blown globes, broken fittings or covers, and switches that are loose, cracked or don't work.
hint.power_points: Look for cracked or loose power points and scorch marks. Note any that don't work if you can test them safely.
hint.wardrobe: Check doors, tracks, shelves, rails and mirrors. Look for broken runners, missing handles and marks inside.
hint.heating_cooling: Note what there is (split system, heater, ceiling fan). Check it turns on and works, and look at the vents, filters and remote.
hint.smoke_alarm: Check there is one and it isn't covered or damaged. Press the test button if you can reach it safely, and note if it's missing or doesn't sound.
hint.mould_damp: Look in corners, on the ceiling, around windows and behind furniture for mould, damp patches or water damage, and note any musty smell.
hint.bed: Check the frame is sturdy. Look at the mattress for stains, tears, sagging and any sign of pests.
hint.bedside_drawers: Open every drawer. Check runners and handles, and look for scratches, water rings and broken parts.
hint.desk_chair: Check they're stable and undamaged. Look for scratches, stains, wobbly legs and broken adjusters.
hint.front_door: Check the door, deadlock and screen door. Try every key, fob and remote you were given, and note how many of each you have.
hint.intercom: Check the intercom or doorbell rings and, if it has one, the door release works.
hint.mailbox: Check the mailbox is undamaged, the lock works and you have the key.
hint.linen_cupboard: Check doors, shelves and handles. Look for damage and any sign of damp or pests inside.
hint.living_furniture: Look for stains, tears, scratches, broken legs and sagging cushions. List anything supplied that's missing.
hint.tv: Check it turns on, has a picture and sound, and the remote works. Look for screen damage.
hint.dining_furniture: Check the table and every chair are stable. Look for scratches, stains, water marks and loose joints.
hint.benchtops: Look for burns, cuts, chips, cracks, stains and lifting edges. Check the silicone along the splashback and sink.
hint.cupboards: Open every cupboard and drawer. Check hinges, handles, shelves and runners, and look for water damage under the sink.
hint.sink: Run the taps hot and cold. Look for drips, leaks, low pressure, slow drainage and damage to the sink.
hint.cooktop_oven: Turn on each burner or element and the oven and grill. Check the knobs, door seal and racks, and note how clean it is.
hint.rangehood: Check the fan and light work, and the filter is in place and clean.
hint.dishwasher: If there is one, check it runs and drains, and the door, seal and racks are undamaged.
hint.fridge: Check it's cold, the door seals are intact, the shelves and drawers are undamaged, and there's no leak or smell.
hint.microwave: Check it heats, the turntable turns and the door closes properly. Note how clean it is.
hint.kitchenware: Note roughly what's supplied, and anything chipped, broken or missing.
hint.shower: Run the shower hot and cold. Check the pressure and drainage, the screen or curtain, and the grout and silicone for mould or gaps.
hint.bath: If there is one, check the taps and drainage, and look for chips, cracks, stains and failed silicone.
hint.basin_vanity: Run the taps. Look for leaks under the basin, slow drainage, cracks and water damage to the vanity.
hint.toilet: Flush it. Check it refills and stops, doesn't leak or keep running, and the seat, lid and cistern are undamaged.
hint.mirror_cabinet: Look for cracks, chips, loose fixings and a damaged backing on the mirror. Check cabinet doors and shelves.
hint.exhaust_fan: Turn it on and check it runs and draws air. Note dust build-up or noise.
hint.towel_rails: Check they're firmly fixed. Note loose, bent or missing ones, and whether a heated rail works.
hint.laundry_tub: Run the taps. Look for leaks, slow drainage and damage to the tub or the cupboard under it.
hint.washer_taps: Check the taps turn and don't drip, and there's somewhere for the machine to drain.
hint.washing_machine: Run a short cycle if you can. Check it fills, drains and spins, and look for leaks and a damaged seal.
hint.dryer: Check it turns on and heats, and the lint filter is in place and clean.
hint.balustrade: Check the railings are firm. Look for loose or rusted parts, cracked glass and gaps.
hint.outdoor_lights: Turn them on. Note blown globes, broken fittings and sensor lights that don't trigger.
hint.drainage: Check drains aren't blocked and water doesn't pool on the surface.
hint.outdoor_furniture: Look for rust, cracks, fading and broken parts. List anything supplied that's missing.
hint.fences_gates: Look for loose or missing palings, leaning sections and damage. Check gates open, close and latch.
hint.lawn_garden: Note how the lawn and garden beds look, including weeds, bare patches and overgrown plants. Photos help here.
hint.paths_driveway: Look for cracks, oil stains, trip hazards and loose pavers.
hint.outdoor_taps: Check each tap turns on and off without dripping or leaking.
hint.clothesline: Check it's firmly fixed, the lines are intact and it folds or turns if it should.
hint.bins: Note which bins there are, and any that are damaged or missing a lid or wheel.
hint.gutters: From the ground, look for overflowing or sagging gutters and loose or broken downpipes. Don't climb up to check.
hint.garage_door: Open and close it with each remote and by hand if it has a release. Look for dents and damage to the tracks.

summary.au_nsw: In New South Wales, tell your landlord or agent about repairs, in writing if you can, and keep a copy. The NSW Government explains which repairs count as urgent and what you can do if an urgent repair isn't fixed. For other repairs, it suggests asking in writing with a clear date. If repairs still aren't done, NSW Fair Trading and the NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal can help. The official pages below have the details.
summary.au_vic: In Victoria, tell your rental provider or agent about repairs, and put non-urgent requests in writing. Consumer Affairs Victoria explains which repairs count as urgent and what you can do if they aren't fixed. If you can't agree, Rental Dispute Resolution Victoria and VCAT can help. The official pages below have the details.
summary.au_qld: In Queensland, tell your landlord or agent about repairs in writing and keep a copy. The Residential Tenancies Authority explains the difference between emergency and routine repairs, and the minimum standards a rental home must meet. If repairs aren't done, the RTA's dispute resolution service and QCAT can help. The official pages below have the details.
summary.au_sa: In South Australia, tell your landlord or agent about urgent repairs as soon as you can, and ask for other repairs in writing. The SA Government explains what counts as urgent and what you can do if a repair isn't done. Consumer and Business Services can give advice, and SACAT can help with disputes. The official pages below have the details.
summary.au_wa: In Western Australia, tell your landlord or agent about repairs in writing. Consumer Protection explains which repairs count as urgent and what you can do if an urgent repair isn't arranged. For other repairs, check with your landlord before arranging anything yourself. The official pages below have the details.
summary.au_tas: In Tasmania, tell your landlord or agent about repairs as soon as you can. Consumer Affairs Tasmania explains the difference between urgent, emergency and general repairs, and what you can do if you can't reach your landlord about an urgent one. It can also help if repairs aren't done. The official pages below have the details.
summary.au_nt: In the Northern Territory, tell your landlord or agent about repairs, and put it in writing to keep a record. The NT Government explains which repairs count as emergency repairs and what you can do if they aren't fixed. NT Consumer Affairs can give advice, and NTCAT can help with disputes. The official pages below have the details.
summary.au_act: In the ACT, tell your lessor or agent about repairs, and put it in writing to keep a record. The ACT Government explains which repairs count as urgent and how you can arrange one if it isn't done. The ACT Civil and Administrative Tribunal can help with disputes. The official pages below have the details.
summary.nz: In New Zealand, tell your landlord about damage or repairs as soon as you can, in writing to keep a record. Tenancy Services explains what to do about urgent repairs and the healthy homes standards. If a problem isn't fixed, you can give your landlord a notice to remedy, and then go to the Tenancy Tribunal. The official pages below have the details.
summary.gb: The rules differ between England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland, and the pages below are for England. Report repairs to your landlord or letting agent, ideally in writing, and keep a copy. GOV.UK explains which repairs it covers and that your local council can help if repairs aren't done or the problem is serious. The official pages below have the details.
